label: Center Vent
description: The center vent is a single vertical slit running up the center back seam, originally derived from equestrian and military tailoring where the split allowed a rider to sit comfortably in the saddle without straining the back of the coat. It is today most closely associated with American tailoring — relaxed, practical, and universally wearable — and sits between the formality of side vents and the slickness of no-vent. The single vent has the minor visual disadvantage of parting and revealing the seat when hands are placed in trouser pockets, but remains the most common construction globally for its simplicity and ease of wear.
